exercise.title: Why is the index letter a placeholder?

statement.p: The sums with index i, k, or r can mean exactly the same addition. In your own words, why does the index disappear after the sum is evaluated, and why is that similar to writing f(x)=x^2 or f(t)=t^2 for the same function?

hint.p: The letter is temporary. It names the slots in the pattern, not a permanent quantity that survives the addition.

exercise.title: Why is sigma notation a name for a finite sum rather than a new idea?

statement.p: The symbol \sum is a compact way to say add all the terms of this pattern. In your own words, why did rectangular estimates force us to want that language, and why is writing \sum_{i=1}^{n} f(x_i)\Delta x not a different computation from writing the sum out by hand?

hint.p: Calculus needs a short name for a finite sum. The pattern is already there; the notation only makes the pattern readable.

exercise.title: Why will the rules for finite sums survive into integrals?

statement.p: Finite sums are linear, they can be split, and they preserve inequalities. In your own words, why should those habits persist when a rectangular sum is taken to a limit, and why is that a reason to learn the sum rules before naming the integral?

hint.p: The integral is born from sums. Linearity, splitting, and order are properties of addition first, and of limits of additions second.

paragraphs.title: Iterating for higher powers
paragraphs.p: This telescoping technique generalizes to any integer power p \ge 1. To find a closed-form formula for \sum_{i=1}^{n} i^p, we start with the binomial expansion of the difference of (p+1)-th powers. Here \binom{N}{k}=N(N-1)\cdots(N-k+1)/(1\cdot2\cdots k) for 1\le k\le N, and \binom{N}{0}=1; these are the coefficients obtained by expanding (k+1)^{p+1} by multiplication:
Summing both sides from k=1 to n telescopes the left side entirely:

Because the right side isolates (p+1)\sum k^p alongside a linear combination of sums of strictly lower degree, we can solve for \sum k^p as long as we have already computed the formulas for all lower powers.
